Reasoning: The stem states that the section form of the valley at P is related to the geostrophic deflection force. This river flows southward, and combined with the lateral-erosion direction of the asymmetrical valley, it can be judged that this place is in the Northern Hemisphere, that is, on the west coast of the continent at about 40°N. In Northern Hemisphere winter, the Eurasian continent cools strongly, and a cold high pressure forms near the ground and mainly controls it.

Figure B is the geological section of the valley at P and its vicinity. The two sides of the section are marked "west" and "east." It can be seen that the valley section is asymmetrical, and it shows a limestone aquifer, groundwater flow direction, and spring.
Reasoning: The stem states that the section form of the valley at P is related to the geostrophic deflection force. This river flows southward, and combined with the lateral-erosion direction of the asymmetrical valley, it can be judged that this place is in the Northern Hemisphere, that is, on the west coast of the continent at about 40°N. The west coast of the continent at about 40°N belongs to the Mediterranean climate, and precipitation is concentrated in winter; winter rain infiltrates and recharges groundwater, so the season when the spring discharge in Figure B is greatest is Northern Hemisphere winter. In Northern Hemisphere winter, the Eurasian continent cools strongly, and a cold high pressure forms near the ground and mainly controls it.
